cards.text: One day an expert in the law, a man who studies God's Law, stands up to test Jesus. 'Teacher,' he asks, 'what must I do to inherit eternal life?' Standing up to test Jesus takes nerve, friend. That's like walking into my bakery to teach ME how to stamp a cookie.

cards.question: An expert in the law asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life. How does Jesus answer him?

answers.text: He asks what the Law says
He tells him to wait and see

cards.text: Jesus asks back, 'What is written in the Law?' and 'How do you read it?' Asking a law expert about the Law is like asking ME about cookies, so pull up a chair, because this man is READY.

cards.question: Jesus asks the expert what the Law says. The expert answers with two commands. What are they about?

answers.text: Loving God and loving your neighbor
Keeping the Sabbath and giving offerings
Honoring parents and telling the truth

cards.text: He answers, 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind' and 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Heart, soul, strength AND mind, friend. That's the whole batch, down to the last crumb.

cards.question: Jesus tells the expert in the law that he answered correctly.
The expert asked how to inherit eternal life. Jesus tells him, 'Do this and you will ___.'

cards.text: Jesus just told him he's right. Case closed? NOPE, because the expert has one more question for Jesus.

cards.question: Jesus told the expert he answered correctly. What does the expert ask Jesus next?

answers.text: And how often should I pray

cards.question: The expert in the law asks Jesus who his neighbor is. Why does he ask?

answers.text: He wants to help his neighbor
He forgot what the Law says

cards.text: I think he was hoping for some fine print. It's like when the boss says 'clean the break room' and somebody raises a hand and asks, 'Okay, but define CLEAN.'
Jesus takes up the expert's question and answers with a story. A man is going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he falls into the hands of robbers.

cards.question: In Jesus' story, the robbers on the road to Jericho take the man's things but leave him unhurt.

cards.text: They strip him, beat him and leave him half dead. Then, by chance, a priest comes down the same road and sees him.

cards.question: A priest sees the man the robbers left half dead. What does the priest do?

answers.text: He passes by on the other side
He runs to the next town for help
He stops and prays over the man

cards.text: The OTHER side, friend. I've done the 'oh, I didn't see you' walk across a parking lot myself, so I'm not throwing any flour.
Next a Levite, from the tribe of Levi that was set apart to assist the priests (Numbers 3:6), comes to that same spot. He sees the man too.

cards.question: The Levite sees the hurt man on the road and stops to help him.

cards.text: Two men passed by. Then a Samaritan, a man from the land of Samaria, comes upon him on a journey, and John's Gospel tells us Jews didn't associate with Samaritans (John 4:9).

cards.question: When the Samaritan sees the man the robbers left half dead, he has ___.
The Samaritan goes to the man, bandages his wounds and pours on oil and wine. Then how does he get the man off the road?

answers.text: He puts him on his own animal
He carries him on his back
He waves down a passing cart

cards.question: The Samaritan puts the hurt man on his own animal. Where does he bring him?
At the inn, the Samaritan takes care of the hurt man himself.

cards.text: His OWN animal, friend, and I won't even lend out my apron. The next day he takes out two denarii and gives them to the innkeeper.

cards.question: The Samaritan gives the innkeeper two denarii. What does he tell the innkeeper?

answers.text: Take care of him and I will repay you
Send him home when he can walk
Find out who did this to him

cards.text: 'Take care of him,' he said, 'and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.' An open tab for a STRANGER, when I've seen a group chat fight for three days over who owes for one box of cookies.
Then Jesus asks the expert, 'Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?'

cards.question: Jesus asks which of the three men was a neighbor to the man the robbers beat. How does the expert in the law answer?

answers.text: The one who showed him mercy
The one who came by first

cards.question: Jesus sends the expert in the law off to show ___ just like the Samaritan did.

cards.text: He asked who his neighbor was, and Jesus told him, 'Go and do likewise.' No fine print on THAT one, friend.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: the setup, the quoted question, 'Standing up to test Jesus takes nerve, friend.' and the bakery joke. The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke compares the wrong action. The expert is testing Jesus with a question, but the comparison is someone coming in to teach Papa Dorin how to stamp. Testing and teaching aren't the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quoted answer, 'Heart, soul, strength AND mind, friend.' and 'That's the whole batch, down to the last crumb.' The limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank quotes Jesus' line, 'Do this and you will ___.', and asks the baker to supply the next word of wording they haven't seen. That makes it a test of wording, not of meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. Of 6 choice cards, 4 are multiple choice, 1 is true or false and 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card says the tribe of Levi was 'set apart to assist the priests' and cites Numbers 3:6. Numbers 3:6 says to present the tribe of Levi to Aaron the priest to assist him. It doesn't say 'set apart,' so the reference doesn't support the fact as stated.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Two men passed by,' which retells Luke 10:31-32. It cites only Luke 10:33, so the citation is too narrow.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
